stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n} \left(x + 3\right)^{n}}{5^{n} \left(n^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3\right)} \) has radius of convergence \( 5 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = -8 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = -8 \) the series converges by direct comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \), because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x + 3\right| < 5 \), so the left endpoint is \( x = -8 \).
At \( x = -8 \), \( \frac{\left(x + 3\right)^{n}}{5^{n}} = \left(\frac{-5}{5}\right)^{n} = (-1)^{n} \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3} \).
The terms are positive and \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3} < \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \), the terms of a convergent p-series with \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).
At \( x = -8 \) the series converges by direct comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \), because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \), so \( x = -8 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = -8 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series threshold reversed, so p greater than 1 read as divergence

options.label: At \( x = -8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3} \) decrease to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test used on the endpoint series although its terms are all positive

options.label: At \( x = -8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the terms \( \frac{(-1)^n}{n^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3} \) alternate and shrink.
options.derivation: the factor (-1)^n produced by substituting the negative displacement -5 dropped, so the endpoint series was tested with the wrong sign pattern
